morningLede: The national market is absorbing its own supply build: the 12-month sold base jumped 10% over 30 days (10,069→11,070) against a 7% rise in actives (11,497→12,337), pulling months-stock down 13.7→13.4 even as listings hit a new high. But the improvement is entirely outside the two biggest overhangs — Victoria pushed to 17.1 months on 6,572 actives (53% of the national book) and Sydney's three growth basins still sit at 28.7–33.7 months — so the national number is now actively misleading about where risk lives.
note: House views written each morning by the desk analyst from last night's run. Income and build-cost figures are APPROXIMATE external benchmarks (label them as such, or verify current figures with web search). Land figures are from the certified RLP dataset.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the freeze holds and remains stratified. Sydney Northwest is the pure strike — 33 months of stock, only 191 of 570 listings priced (34%), asking $2,410 against $2,342/m² on the thin priced tail. Sydney Southwest asks $2,107 vs $1,511/m² certified (+39%) at 28.7 months, while Sydney South West has converged to honest pricing ($2,196 vs $2,084, a 5% gap) yet still carries 33.7 months on 264 annual sales — honest pricing alone doesn't clear a market this deep at $725k medians. NSW's headline months-stock improvement (16.5→15.3 over 30 days) is mix and denominator, not basin repricing.
houseViews.falsifier: Basin priced-share rising above 60% (Northwest especially) alongside corridor months-stock falling below 20 on rising sold counts.

houseViews.view: Maintained: VIC is the only major market where the overhang is still building — 16.9→17.1 months over 30 days with actives up 6,368→6,572 — but it remains the only deep market that is honestly priced: 95% of listings carry a price and the ask-to-sold gap is a workable 13% ($841 vs $742/m²) versus Sydney's up-to-39%. Cheap ($394k median), abundant, and screenable keeps VIC the mechanical landing zone for the late-2026 investor rotation; the overhang caps price growth but the fringe corridors (Melbourne North 20.9 months on 488 sales, Northwest 16.1 on 532) are digesting, not frozen.
houseViews.falsifier: VIC months-stock pushing past 20 with sold 12m rolling below ~4,000, or new-listing absorption failing to lift by Q1 2027.

houseViews.view: New: split the true VIC distress out from fringe digestion — Melbourne Peri-Urban at 38.5 months on just 125 annual sales, South Gippsland 33.1 on 100, Gippsland 26.2 on 66, West Gippsland 20.8 on 144. These are demand deserts, not overpriced markets: asking-to-sold gaps run 12–25% ($350k vs $508/m² sold in Peri-Urban, $628 asked vs $504 sold in South Gippsland) and the buyer pool that stretched to acreage in 2021-22 has evaporated. Mechanism: with metro fringe lots at $394k and 17 months of choice, there is no scarcity premium left for the 644-772m² lifestyle lot an hour further out. Avoid englobo and stage stock across the belt; this clears last.
houseViews.falsifier: Belt sold volumes rising 50%+ per window, or peri-urban months-stock falling below 25 without listings simply being withdrawn.

houseViews.view: Maintained: capitulation clears — Torquay's decline is decelerating (-13.5% prior year → -5.9% last 12m) with volume at 43 sales in the latest window versus 9 three years ago; Winchelsea cut -11.8% and printed 21 sales. Contrast Portarlington (-27.3% over 3yrs, 10 sales) and San Remo (-25.9%, 15 sales) where the adjustment is incomplete and vendors still hold 2022 rates. The bottom in the priced coastal names is forming; the unpriced holdouts have another leg down.
houseViews.falsifier: Torquay/coastal volumes falling back below ~15 per window, or price declines re-accelerating past -10% in the next windows.

houseViews.view: Maintained with rising conviction: the national sold base up 10% in 30 days (10,069→11,070 12m-rolling) while months-stock fell despite a 7% listings build is exactly the early-positioning footprint we'd expect ahead of the 1 Jul 2027 changes (negative gearing narrowed to new builds, CGT discount replaced by indexation). The bid lands where product is priced and cheap — VIC (95% priced, $394k) and outer QLD/SA — not Sydney basins where 66% of Northwest stock cannot be screened. Tight markets (SA 6.2 months, WA 7.9, Adelaide North 5.4) get the price inflation; loose priced markets get the volume.
houseViews.falsifier: No pickup in investor-share of land sales or VIC/QLD new-listing absorption by Q1 2027, or policy amendment before commencement.

houseViews.view: Maintained: tightness is genuine — 6.2 months statewide, Adelaide North clearing at ask ($914 asking vs $910 sold $/m², 5.4 months), a zero-negotiation market — but the headline sold-$/m² growth remains composition-inflated (one estate ≈ a third of 2026 sales; like-for-like ≈ +9.5%). The affordability ceiling is the central mechanism: $420k median in the historically cheap state, defended almost entirely via lot compression (Roseworthy -47% lot size over 3yrs, Mount Barker -27%, Morphett Vale -33%, Australind-style shrinkage across the rocketship list). Compression is the market's confession that the gross-price ceiling binds; while stock holds near 6 months the path is deceleration, not correction, and the 2027 investor rotation delays the reckoning.
houseViews.falsifier: Stock above 10 months, incentive share rising two runs in a row, or lot compression stalling while sales volumes fall.

houseViews.view: Maintained at high conviction: $/m² accelerating into the ceiling — +49.7% then +99.6% to $1,027/m² (vs $344 three years ago) while lots compressed another 38% in one year and volume thinned 79→45→35 sales per window. A market doubling its rate while shrinking the product a third on falling volume is borrowing from the price ceiling, not raising it. Sell stage stock into this rate; do not underwrite englobo at $1,027/m² residuals.
houseViews.falsifier: Lot sizes stabilising while $/m² keeps rising on volume recovering above ~50 sales per window.

houseViews.view: New: a distinct hazard class inside the movers — headline $/m² surges printed on collapsing volume. Greenbank is +56.6% last 12m to $1,373/m² on 6 sales, down from 76 three years ago; Virginia is +72.9% to $1,120/m² on 8 sales, down from 48. Mechanism: when a corridor sells out its affordable stages, the surviving sales skew premium and the $/m² series marks up on selection, not demand — the opposite of Mount Barker, which printed +61% on 90 sales and is a real signal. Do not underwrite feasibilities off the thin prints; treat any window under ~15 sales as unpriceable.
houseViews.falsifier: Greenbank/Virginia volumes recovering above ~20 per window with $/m² holding, which would convert the prints from mix artefact to genuine repricing.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the late-cycle collision is intact — listings up 21% in 30 days (607→732, the largest proportional build of any state) into a market still tight at 7.9 months, with asking $/m² up $1,000→$1,041 against $867 sold (a 20% gap vendors are pricing forward). Mandurah is the accelerating rocketship (+24.4% then +98.6% to $842/m², lots -35% over 3yrs) while Hilbert and Australind show fading second derivatives (59→27% and 53→43%). The tight-supply story holds for now, but developers rushing stock while vendors price the next leg is how tight markets end; the marginal dollar chasing satellites is late money.
houseViews.falsifier: WA months-stock rising above 10, or rocketship windows where lot compression continues but sold $/m² growth drops below 10%.

houseViews.view: Maintained: the state series remains contaminated by the 7-Jul universe expansion (948→1,022 suburbs) — the 30-day 'crash' (asking $539k→$478k, $/m² $1,029→$710, actives 758→1,056) is regional QLD (Townsville $305k at 8.8 months, Gympie, Kingaroy) entering the sample, not repricing. Corridor and suburb evidence says the underlying market is firm at 8.9 months statewide: South Ripley +82% last 12m to $1,774/m² on rising quality of demand, Bahrs Scrub +53% to $1,319/m² on stable 16-23 sale windows. Screen QLD at corridor level until the new-suburb history matures.
houseViews.falsifier: Like-for-like (pre-expansion suburb set) QLD asking or sold $/m² actually falling on the next monthly comparison.

policyCalendar.event: Negative gearing restricted to NEW BUILDS only; CGT 50% discount replaced by indexation (new-build investors keep choice). Expected to rotate investor demand toward new land/dwellings from late 2026.
Gifford Hill (Murray Bridge SA) first ~1,000 lots targeted for release, pending code amendment.
